title: December 1685 Deed
summary: The December 1685 record describes John Mahue selling Governor Thomas Dongan a patent to a large Moriches tract between the Forge and Seatuck rivers. It was a sale to Dongan, not a colonial patent issued to Mahue, and the surviving record does not state the payment amount.
activity_update_summary: Added a cited introduction explaining the December 1685 Moriches sale, Mahue's 1687 patent requests, and Wyangonhott's 1703 testimony; corrected the site's mismatched page references and connected three Historic Moments.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Unkechaug Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: A colonial deed can identify the parties and land that the colonial legal system recognized, but it cannot by itself show equal power or the full Unkechaug understanding of the transaction. Mahue's 1687 patent requests and Wyangonhott's 1703 testimony show that Unkechaug land authority and efforts to protect land continued after the sale.
introduction_title: A sale, later petitions, and testimony
introduction_content: The December 1685 record concerns John Mahue selling Governor Thomas Dongan a patent to land; it was not a colonial patent issued to Mahue. John A. Strong describes the transaction as covering a large Moriches tract between the Forge and Seatuck rivers, for an unnamed payment. The tract enclosed smaller parcels Mahue had already conveyed, but the surviving record does not state what Dongan paid. Strong places the transaction within a wider pattern of unequal land and labor relations: earlier that year, Mahue had entered a three-month indenture with an East Hampton employer. In late spring 1687, Mahue, Suscaneman, and Tackapousha asked Dongan for patents to small parcels; Strong reports that Dongan granted all three requests. After Mahue's death, Unkechaug sachem Wyangonhott testified on August 21, 1703, that Mahue had held the right to sell the Moriches lands. Read together, these records show sale, petition, and testimony—not a single neutral document that explains all Unkechaug relationships to this land.
